transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you and what brings you in today?

I guess… my body’s been kind of all over the place. For a while I couldn’t sit still, I was pacing around the apartment all night, writing notes for this supper-club idea. And now it’s the opposite. I feel really slowed down. My sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident, even if others around you didn’t see it that way?

Yeah… I guess so. After I got fired, I felt strangely… unstoppable, like everything was about to work out and I had all these plans. But if people questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get really angry. Like they were trying to wreck everything.
Have there been times when your mood or energy level caused problems at work, home, or in relationships, or when someone suggested you needed help or hospitalization?

Yeah… it’s caused problems. I haven’t really been able to keep work plans straight, or rent stuff, or things I said I’d do for my family.

My sister ended up taking me to a crisis clinic because I just… couldn’t get basic responsibilities organized by myself. I didn’t really want to go, but she said I needed help.
How long did those periods of high energy or feeling unstoppable usually last? Was it days or weeks?
It was more than just a few days. I guess… it’s been going on about four months, since I got fired from the restaurant.
During that time when you felt unstoppable and full of ideas, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual, or maybe even felt rested after just a few hours of sleep?
I’m not really sure. I mean… my sleep wasn’t exactly normal, but I don’t know if I’d say I felt rested after only a few hours. I didn’t keep track of it.
Can you think back to when you felt unstoppable—was there a time during that period when your mood was so high or irritable that it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

Yeah… after I got fired, I did feel kind of weirdly unstoppable. Like excited, like I had all these plans.

But if someone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get really angry. Like… way more than usual. It felt like they were trying to ruin everything.
Can you recall if there was a time when your mood was consistently high, irritable, or agitated for at least several days in a row, clearly different from your usual self?

Yeah… I mean, after I got fired it was like that for days at a time. I felt weirdly unstoppable, excited, like I had all these plans. But if anyone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d just… blow up. Like they were trying to ruin everything.
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was clearly and consistently different from usual—like unusually high, overly confident, or irritable—for at least a week straight?

Yeah… I think so. After I got fired, it went on like that for about a week, maybe more. I felt kind of unstoppable, like my plans all made sense. But if anyone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d just blow up at them… like they were trying to ruin everything.
During that time when you felt unstoppable, did you notice that you were talking much more quickly than usual, or that your thoughts were racing so fast you couldn’t keep up?
Yeah… my thoughts were moving really fast. I’d go from, like, recipes to a logo, then investors, then renting a space… and each idea would set off more. It was hard to shut it off.

During the time you felt unstoppable and full of ideas, did you find yourself doing a lot more things than usual—like starting a bunch of new projects, making a lot of plans, or moving around constantly even if it wasn’t productive?

Yeah… I was doing a lot. I kept texting old coworkers, making spreadsheets, trying to set up tastings, contacting musicians… trying to recruit people. It was kind of all day and night, like the supper club had to happen right then.

During the time you felt unstoppable and full of ideas, did you find yourself getting involved in a lot of pleasurable activities that had the potential to cause problems—like spending sprees, risky investments, or impulsive decisions?
I don’t know… I mean, I don’t think I did anything like that. Nothing I’d really call a spree or anything. I was just… focused on the idea, I guess.
After that period when you felt unstoppable and full of ideas, did you experience a time when you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping or eating?

Yeah… mostly I just don’t really care about things right now. Like cooking, taking food photos, music, soccer… even volunteering. Stuff that usually keeps me kind of steady just feels flat. I know I used to be into it, I just… can’t really feel it.
Did you have a period of at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, it’s been more like everything feels flat. Cooking, music, soccer, volunteering… stuff I usually care about. I know I used to enjoy it, I just can’t really make myself feel it right now.
Did you have a period of at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. It’s mostly that the things that usually keep me steady—cooking, music, pickup soccer, volunteering—just feel kind of empty now. Like I remember caring about them, but I can’t really feel it.
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was clearly and consistently different from usual—like unusually high, overly confident, or irritable—for at least one full week?

Yeah… after I got fired, I was kind of… unusually wired, I guess. I felt really unstoppable, like I had all these plans. And if anyone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get really angry, like they were trying to wreck everything.

During that time when you felt unstoppable and overly confident, did you have any experiences where you believed things that weren’t true, like having special powers, being destined for greatness, or that people were trying to harm you?

Yeah… I guess. I really believed I was about to make this bilingual supper club into the best one in the city. Like investors would be idiots not to back me… even though I didn’t have a job or any money lined up.

During that time when you felt unstoppable, did you ever believe something strongly that others might not have agreed was true—like you had a special connection, a unique mission, or that something was definitely going to happen even without clear evidence?

Yeah… I mean, I was sure the supper club thing was going to be huge. Like, the best bilingual supper club in the city. I really thought investors would be stupid not to back me, even though… I didn’t have a job or money set up.
